Second, the barrier $\kappa\le\frac13$ reduces to irreducible isogeny factors; the archimedean branch is closed by the unconditional Theorem 8.7 of 2610.00544v2, and the remaining input $R_\rho\le3$ for general $\mathrm{GL}_2$ and non-$\mathrm{GL}_2$ towers is shown to be not derivable from the currently proved inputs, the obstruction being isolated in an explicit saturating model with $R\equiv4$, $\kappa\to\frac{5}{12}$. Third, the conductor--discriminant constant is not universal: inside the CM class it forms the continuum $(q^2+2q+3)/(q^2-1)$, and the mixed-prime model $u^{p^n}+v^{q^m}=1$ contributes the new continuum $[-\frac{2}{p-1},-\frac{2}{q-1}]$ with $\Lambda^{(a)}=0$ exactly. On the Fermat tower the normalisation $\hat f_n=(2n+1)\log p$, the exact layer remainder $u_n$, $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{ar}}=-2w/(2n+1)+O(p^{-n}/n)$ and the closed form for $R_n$ are derived by finite computation with a two-channel cross-check. The upper half of Problem 10.12 is closed inside the whole Kummer family; the single-curve interior realisation (I'b) and the general bound $R\le3$ (route II) remain open. The remaining Mumford-type danger class is then evaluated explicitly (rounds 78--88): the rank-three criterion and the alignment with arXiv:2406.19785 record five exact structures with three retractions; equality-case constructions are rigid; the finite-layer band is continuous with $\gamma=4-\frac32\mu$; the $\mathrm{End}^0$ MT-group classification leaves genus 4 as the sole survivor, realised by the explicit curve $C_{7,t}$; and all 58 degree-eight CM anchor fields of arXiv:2510.00093v2 are certified to have Galois group identifier 8T13, with 8T24 occurring zero times, closing the 8T24 path ($\Lambda\equiv0$) and the long-term search items. In the final rounds 89--100 the last-mile chain is run to its end: $C_{7,t}$ is realised with explicit MT structure, CM companion and conductor formula, and the characteristic-two analysis strips the remaining finite layers $3,6,12,24$, forcing tower exhaustion; a full literature-cut proof attempt of the characteristic is recorded and fails at an explicit sign barrier, leaving a conditional theorem with three propositions; the sign of $\gamma_A$ is settled by a three-valued judgement ($1274/1274$ sample points positive), with $\delta_\gamma=48c/L=12\delta_\kappa$; and the CM anchor double-point calibration reduces the surviving input of route (II) to the single sign $\Delta\Phi_{\mathrm{eff}}>0$, with all 58 endpoints satisfying $d_\Phi=n^2$. Route (II) remains open, conditioned on this single input. Nothing in this paper proves $abc$; Theorem A of the source texts is an external input and is not independently verified here.

papers.title: Topology of some smooth real Fano threefolds arising from blow-ups along rational curves
papers.abstract: We describe the topological blow-up of a fibre of a Seifert fibration. We then apply this result to determine the diffeomorphism types of the real loci of smooth real Fano threefolds obtained by blowing up either $\mathbb{P}^3_{\mathbb{R}}$ or a smooth real quadric threefold along a smooth real rational curve. As an application, we also determine the topology of the real loci of the two real forms of the quintic del Pezzo threefold $V_5$, completing the topological classification of smooth real rational del Pezzo threefolds.

papers.title: Tropical Matsusaka and Matsusaka--Ran Criteria
papers.abstract:
The tropical Schottky problem asks which principally polarized tropical abelian varieties are isomorphic to tropical Jacobian varieties equipped with their canonical principal polarizations. We prove the tropical Matsusaka criterion and the tropical Matsusaka--Ran criterion, which are the main results of this paper, and show that their hypotheses are equivalent. Together with the tropical Poincar\'e formula proved by Gross--Shokrieh, these results give a geometric solution to the tropical Schottky problem. In particular, we give an affirmative answer to a question posed by Brannetti--Melo--Viviani.
  Several tools are developed for the proofs of the two criteria. In particular, we establish Hodge-type inequalities for ample tropical Cartier divisors on tropical abelian varieties and prove a splitting criterion for principally polarized tropical abelian varieties.

papers.title: Uniform Spectral Gap for the AKLT Model on the Square Lattice
papers.abstract: We prove that the spin-$2$ AKLT Hamiltonian on the square-lattice torus has a unique ground state and a spectral gap bounded below uniformly when both side lengths are sufficiently large, as expected since the work of Affleck, Kennedy, Lieb, and Tasaki. We also prove uniqueness of the infinite-volume frustration-free state on the square lattice. We first bound the quantum gap from below by the spectral gap of a classical block dynamics for the measure that the valence-bond-solid state defines in spin coherent states. We bound the latter through the coupling argument of Martinelli, Olivieri, and Schonmann, whose input we derive from the exponential decay of responses of pair correlations to boundary conditions. We prove this decay by an expansion into bond-self-avoiding walks, comparing the expansions with and without boundary conditions walk by walk, and closing the resulting inequality as a contraction. The proof is computer-assisted. Its local and combinatorial inputs are verified in exact integer arithmetic and in floating-point arithmetic with directed rounding.

papers.title: Unique continuation for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: We prove a unique continuation property for eigenstates of the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian, viewed as functions of the electron configuration with values in the spin-photon space. The vector potential may lie in $L^6_\mathrm{loc}$, with its divergence, curl, and the scalar potential in $L^p_\mathrm{loc}$ for some $p>2$. As an application, we prove a Hohenberg-Kohn theorem at positive coupling strength: the spin-summed ground-state density and combined current density determine the external potentials up to a gauge transformation and an additive constant.

papers.title: Virasoro elements in conformal algebras
papers.abstract: It is well known that Virasoro elements play an extremely important role in the theory of vertex operator algebras, and likewise a very significant role in the field of conformal algebras. In this paper, we introduce the notion of a regular action in the category of conformal modules over Lie conformal algebras with Virasoro elements. We show that a finite conformal module over the general conformal algebra $\mathfrak{gc}_1$ (resp., $\mathfrak{gc}_N$ with $N\ge2$) is semisimple if and only if there exists a pair of different Virasoro elements (resp., canonical Virasoro elements) with regular actions. Along the way to finding semisimplicity criteria, we also discuss the classification of Virasoro elements of $\mathfrak{gc}_N$ in-depth, leading us to construct a huge number of new Virasoro conformal modules.
